newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Old Mutual sees only one rate cut in '97.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Old Mutual sees only one rate cut in '97.

text.p: Strong money supply growth and private sector credit extension made it likely that there would be only one interest rate cut this year, Old Mutual Unit Trust gilt fund manager Mark le Roux said on Tuesday.
In a statement, Le Roux said that the cut was only likely to take place in the second half of the year.
Analysts had previously been forecasting at least two interest rate cuts this year.

"While structurally Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's first budget has put us in tandem with the global trend of lower deficits, the surprisingly strong economic growth will limit the downside of interest rates in the short term," Le Roux said.
"It now seems likely that there will be only one rate cut this year."

Any rate cut in the face of the better than expected growth in the economy could fuel further credit demand, leading to a weakening of the balance of payments and undermine the rand's recent strength.
Credit extension to the private sector grew at a year-on-year rate of 17.34 percent in February from 17.06 percent in January.

Long bonds, currently at 15 percent, were in "neutral" territory after the sharp 150 point decline from the 16 percent level. This had been followed by a 50 point retracement reflecting concerns over the economy's strength and the higher pattern of U.S. rates.
"In the U.S., the (Federal Reserve) has raised rates by 25 points reflecting stronger than expected U.S. economic growth," he said.
"If rates there rise further, South African bond rates could move up in line with them."
He said the structural changes introduced in the March budget had been well received by local and foreign investors, as had new moves on the privatisation of state corporations.
The expected inflow of $1.3 billion following the partial privatisation of Telkom would be bullish for the rand and the bond market, Le Roux added.
